verdict: APPROVED. The delta touches only TerminalLauncher::identity and adds two tests. The instance becomes lowercase_hex(counter, 4 digits) + session[0:44], with the counter limited to 1-0xffff, and exhaustion or overflow is refused before any state change, directory or spawn. This fixes the real caption collision: in 003 every app's 'Terminal <instance[0:12]>' showed the same session prefix. Now the visible prefixes differ per app (for example 000101234567 and 000201234567). The full 48-hex identity, the app CLI, CHONKTERM/1, HID, commands, readiness and cleanup are unchanged. A title is only a visual label, never process or input authority.

binding.replay: verify_checkpoint.py (temp dir in scratch): 'Verified004 cumulative 23 and incremental 1 files, full tree and dependencies'. The 003 receipt recomputes as cdc2096c497f5bd7 (unchanged).
binding.delta: from-003.patch changes only crates/wm-darwin/src/terminal_launch.rs: a MAX_INSTANCE_COUNTER constant, the identity() body and two tests. All other source bytes equal 003.

checks.allocation: next = self.next.checked_add(1) filtered to at most 0xffff, else 'instance counter exhausted'. The Instance is built with format!("{next:04x}{}", &session[..44]) and validated by Instance::parse, and only then is self.next assigned. A refusal therefore never advances the counter, and u64::MAX cannot wrap.
checks.uniqueness: Within one launcher, counters 1-65535 are distinct, so both the full instances and the 12-hex visible prefixes (counter + session[0:8]) are distinct. Across sessions, uniqueness rests on the fresh host-selected session nonce, which now keeps 176 bits in the instance (003 kept 128). Per-instance record directories are still created exclusively with mkdirat, so a collision would be refused, not reused.
checks.no_reuse_after_failure: request() still calls identity() first and only then begins the audit and prepare. A failed preparation or spawn consumes that counter value, matching the layout's 'no reuse after failed launch'.
checks.layout_contract: I recomputed INSTANCE_LAYOUT.json: all three vectors (counters 1, 2 and 65535) give exactly the stated instance and title. Its application_source_evidence hashes match app revision 002's main.rs (bb82f9f2) and pty.rs (292a213e), and rev002 main.rs:446 still sets the title as 'Terminal ' + instance[0:12], so the caption derivation is the app's unchanged code.
checks.tests: first_two_instances_have_distinct_visible_prefixes_and_exact_full_ids checks the exact IDs, distinct prefixes, the 44-hex suffix, and that the CLI argument and record directory use the same full ID with no child created. four_hex_counter_accepts_last_value_then_refuses_without_wrap_or_side_effects checks that ffff is accepted, then the 0xffff and u64::MAX states are refused without advancing, with no application, audit attempt or directory created.

host_evidence.serial: The recorded serial run (--test-threads=1) passes 54 library tests, 5 Wayland tests and both new identity tests.
host_evidence.parallel_failure_preserved: The recorded parallel run exits 101 with 53 passed and 1 failed: hid::tests::open_flags_character_rejection_and_nofollow_do_not_use_hid_nodes, a fd_closed(fd) assertion. That baseline test checks a numeric descriptor after close, which concurrent tests can reuse, so it can fail falsely in parallel. The HID source is unchanged and the excerpt is kept as a failure, not reclassified. I accept that explanation for this identity-only delta, but the test stays order-sensitive until it stops checking reusable descriptor numbers.
